abstract: As cloud production becomes an integral part of broadcasters’ live workflows, the corresponding cloud infrastructure becomes an integral part of the media transport network. Cloud infrastructure providers, often public in nature, are accessible either through the public internet or through leased lines. Regardless of public or private, experience shows that these connections are not up to the quality standards required for low latency live streaming media, making quality-enhancing technologies, such as retransmission or Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ), an imperative part of the network infrastructure to deliver on the requirements for broadcast quality transmission. Two solutions have emerged as front runners on the quest for the next de facto standard for broadcast retransmission—Reliable Internet Stream Transport (RIST) and Secure Reliable Transport (SRT). This report compares these two alternatives from a theoretical and performance perspective and compares them with a commercial reference alternative.

authors.bio: Mikael Wånggren holds a master’s degree in electrical engineering from the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH), Stockholm, Sweden. He started his career as an embedded software developer for a realtime operating system widely used in the telecommunications industry. In 2012, he joined Net Insight, Stockholm, Sweden, where he was part of starting up their Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ)-based internet media transport product line, and he has had the opportunity to witness the then still nascent market segment grow exponentially since then. Currently, he is product owner for the in-house developed ARQ protocols. He is an active member of the RIST Activity Group within the VSF as well as a keen observer of SRT progress.
authors.name: Mikael Wånggren

authors.bio: Love Thyresson received a bachelor’s degree in computer science from Örebro University, Örebro, Sweden, and a master’s degree in computer science from Linköping University, Linköping, Sweden. After spending the earlier part of his career in various strategic product manager roles at Ericsson, Stockholm, Sweden and San Jose, CA, in fields such as mobile backhaul and network management systems, he joined Net Insight in 2014 to head up the internet media transport business. Under his leadership, this relatively untried market segment has grown rapidly and proved itself to be an indispensable tool in modern media communications. Since the original publication of this article, Thyresson has left Net Insight for new opportunities outside of the media industry.
